hints: Look closely at the slope of the curve just after P and just after R. At P the ventricular volume starts to fall sharply, at R it starts to rise again.

Remember valves close to prevent backflow when pressure on the forward side drops. Think about which valve must shut when ventricles start to squeeze, and which must shut when ventricles stop squeezing.
walkthrough:
**Read what the graph is really showing**

Look at the y-axis. It is volume of ventricles, not pressure. When the line goes down, blood is leaving the ventricles. When it goes up, blood is filling the ventricles.

After P the line falls, so ventricles are emptying. After R the line rises, so ventricles are filling.

**Work out the AV valve at P**

P is right at the start of ventricular systole. The ventricles are about to contract hard to push blood out.

To stop blood being pushed backwards into the atria, the atrioventricular valves must shut. So at P, the AV valve closes. That gives the first heart sound.

**Work out the semilunar valve at R**

R is right at the end of ventricular systole, at the lowest ventricular volume. The ventricles have finished emptying and now relax for diastole.

As ventricular pressure falls below the pressure in the aorta and pulmonary artery, the semilunar valves snap shut to stop backflow into the ventricles. So at R, the semilunar valve closes. That gives the second heart sound.

options.A: Correct. AV valve closes at start of ventricular systole (P) to prevent atrial backflow, and semilunar valve closes at end of ventricular systole (R) to prevent arterial backflow.
options.B: Half right. AV valve does close at P, but semilunar valve does not open at R. It closes because ventricular pressure is falling for diastole.
options.C: Half right. Semilunar valve does close at R, but AV valve does not open at P. It must close so contracting ventricles do not push blood back to the atria.
options.D: Both wrong. Neither valve opens at these points. P marks the start of ejection so AV closes, R marks the end of ejection so semilunar closes.
